Power of a planned uSDT study

Source: R/power.R
usdt_power.Rd

Computes the power of the tests of the three uSDT hypotheses, the difference between mean sensitivities (H1), their correlation (H2) and the latent regression (H3), for a study that samples a given number of subjects, each with a given number of trials per task, from a population described by usdt_population().

Usage

usdt_power(
  population,
  subjects,
  trials,
  hypothesis = c("diff = 0", "rho = 0", "intercept = 0"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  signal = 0.5,
  dichotomize = c("none", "influence", "awareness", "both"),
  combine = c("each", "all"),
  method = c("approximate", "simulation"),
  nsim = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  ncores = 1L,
  progress = interactive()
)

# S3 method for class 'usdt_power'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'usdt_power'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.usdt_power'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

Arguments

population

A usdt_population object from usdt_population(). With several scenarios, the power of each. It can also be a usdt_plan from usdt_plan(), whose designs, hypotheses and settings are then used, so that usdt_power(plan, method = "simulation") checks a plan. subjects and trials are then left out.

subjects

Number of subjects. Several values give one design each.

trials

Number of trials per subject in each task, signal and noise trials together: one value for both tasks, or one for each as c(awareness = , influence = ) or list(awareness = , influence = ). Several values give one design each. A value shared by both tasks keeps them equal, and values given for each task are crossed.

hypothesis

Character vector of hypotheses, written as in usdt_equivalence(): "<quantity> <op> <value>" with the quantity diff, rho, slope or intercept and the operator =, < or >, or "<quantity> in [a, b]" and "<quantity> out [a, b]". The default tests the three point nulls that hsdt() reports.

alpha

Significance level of every test, between 0 and 0.5 (default 0.05).

signal

Proportion of signal trials in each task (default 0.5), one value for both tasks or one for each. Each task must have a whole number of signal and of noise trials.

dichotomize

Which tasks are split at the median, as in usdt_data_tasks(): "none", "influence", "awareness", "both", or one logical value for each task. The split fixes the criterion of a task at zero, so its criterion values in population are not used.

combine

"each" reports the power of each hypothesis. "all" also reports the probability that every one of them rejects H0 in the same study.

method

"approximate" (the default) computes power from the sampling distribution of the estimates, in seconds. "simulation" simulates whole studies and analyses each one with hsdt(), which takes minutes. See Details.

nsim

Number of simulated studies for each scenario and design (default 1000). Simulation only.

seed

Random seed of the simulated studies. With the default NULL, the seed is drawn from the current random number stream. Simulation only.

ncores

Number of CPU cores. Values above 1 fit the simulated studies in parallel on a temporary cluster, which works on Windows, macOS and Linux and stops when the run ends. Simulation only.

progress

Logical. Show the expected duration and a progress bar (default TRUE in interactive sessions). Simulation only.

x

A usdt_power object.

digits

Number of decimals printed.

...

Ignored.

object

A usdt_power object from a simulation.

Value

An object of class usdt_power: a data frame with one row per scenario, design and hypothesis, and the columns scenario, subjects, trials_awareness, trials_influence, hypothesis, test, H1, H0, true (the population value of the tested quantity), se (its expected standard error), power, estimable (the share of studies in which the analysis can estimate it), in_null (whether the population lies in H0, so that power is the type I error rate), and reliability_awareness and reliability_influence. A simulation adds mc_se, the Monte Carlo standard error of power, and power.low and power.high, its 95% Wilson interval. With combine = "all", a row per scenario and design whose hypothesis is "all" gives the joint power. It prints one report for a single design and a table for several.

For a simulation, summary() reports the precision of each quantity across the simulated studies that estimate it: the mean estimate, its bias, the empirical standard error (the SD of the estimates), the mean standard error the fits report, the mean width of the intervals and their coverage of the population value.

The approximation

Each subject's estimated \(d'\) is treated as its true \(d'\) plus a measurement error. The variance of that error, \(v\), is the one usdt_reliability() reports, averaged over the subjects of the population: it falls with the number of trials and grows with extreme rates. The observed \(d'\) of the subjects then have covariance \(S = \Sigma + \mathrm{diag}(v_A, v_I)\), where \(\Sigma\) is the covariance of the population, and the reliability of each task is \(\sigma^2 / (\sigma^2 + v)\). Trials act on the tests only through \(v\), and subjects through their number \(N\).

With \(N\) subjects, the sample mean of their \(d'\) is normal with covariance \(S / N\) and their sample covariance has a Wishart distribution. usdt_power() draws both 20,000 times, subtracts the error variance to estimate \(\Sigma\), and in each draw runs every test as the fitted model would, with the standard errors it would compute at those estimates. Power is the share of draws that reject H0, with a Monte Carlo error of at most 0.004. The draws are the same for every design, so power changes smoothly with the design, and they do not change the random number stream of the session.

A draw whose estimated covariance of the sensitivities is not positive definite (a variance of zero or a correlation of -1 or 1) is a fit on the boundary. There, the fitted model reports the difference but marks the correlation, slope and intercept as not estimable, so the draw counts as a failure to reject them, and estimable reports how often that happens. With an awareness task of low reliability \(R_A\), this probability is close to \(\Phi(-R_A \sqrt{N / 2})\), and more awareness trials lower it faster than more subjects.

The tests

Each hypothesis is decided as the analysis would decide it: "rho = 0" and "slope = 0" by the test on the covariance of usdt_tests(), and every other statement by the tests of usdt_equivalence(), with the correlation on the Fisher-\(z\) scale. se is the standard error at the population values. When the population value lies in H0, power is the type I error rate, and the report says so.

Limits of the approximation

The approximation assumes the equal-variance model that hsdt() fits, so every sd_signal of population must be 1, and it assumes the estimated standard deviations of the criteria stay away from zero. It follows the fitted model closely when the reliability of both tasks is moderate or high. When the awareness task is unreliable, boundary fits are more frequent in the fitted model than here, and the power of H2 and H3 is somewhat optimistic.

Simulation

With method = "simulation", each study draws its subjects from the population and their trials from their d' and criteria. A task split at the median draws one latent score per trial and is split with meyen_split(), as response times would be. Any other task draws binomial counts. The study is then analysed by hsdt() with the confidence level 1 - alpha, and each hypothesis is decided as in the approximation. A fit that fails, or that cannot estimate the quantity, counts as a failure to reject. Each study has its own random number stream, derived from seed, so a run gives the same studies whatever ncores, and every design uses the same streams, which makes the differences between designs less noisy than their Monte Carlo errors suggest. The simulation also accepts a population with unequal variances (sd_signal other than 1), whose studies are then analysed with the equal-variance model. se and the reliabilities are then NA.

A simulation is slow, about a second per study with 100 subjects, so it is best kept for checking a design chosen with the approximation, with enough studies to bound the Monte Carlo error: 1000 studies give an error of at most 0.016.

See also

usdt_population(), usdt_tests(), usdt_equivalence(), usdt_reliability()

Examples

pop <- usdt_population(dprime    = c(awareness = 0.15, influence = 0.30),
                       sd_dprime = c(awareness = 0.35, influence = 0.30),
                       cor_dprime = 0.3, criterion = 0.1)

# 80 subjects, 64 awareness trials and 200 influence trials split at the
# median
usdt_power(pop, subjects = 80, trials = c(awareness = 64, influence = 200),
           dichotomize = "influence")
#> ── Power ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── approximate ── 
#> 
#>   Design       80 subjects; trials per subject: 64 Awareness, 200 Influence (split at the median)
#>   Reliability  Awareness 0.543, Influence 0.738
#> 
#>   Hypothesis        Test              True      SE  Estimable   Power
#>   H1 Δd' = 0        Two-sided test   0.150   0.060      1.000   0.712
#>   H2 rho = 0        Two-sided test   0.300   0.168      1.000   0.379
#>   H3 intercept = 0  Two-sided test   0.261   0.045      1.000   0.992
#> 
#>   Approximate power: the share of 20,000 draws of the subjects' sample
#>   mean and covariance in which the test rejects H0, at alpha = 0.05.

# Several numbers of subjects, and one-sided and equivalence tests
usdt_power(pop, subjects = c(40, 80, 160),
           trials = c(awareness = 64, influence = 200),
           hypothesis = c("diff > 0", "intercept > 0", "rho in [-0.1, 0.1]"),
           dichotomize = "influence")
#> ── Power ──────────────────────────────────────────── approximate · 3 designs ── 
#> 
#>   H1: Δd' > 0, one-sided test
#>   H3: intercept > 0, one-sided test
#>   H2: rho in [-0.1, 0.1], equivalence test (TOST)
#> 
#>   Subjects  Awareness  Influence  Δd' > 0   intercept > 0   rho in [-0.1, 0.1] 
#>         40         64        200    0.562           0.935                0.000^
#>         80         64        200    0.809           0.995                0.000^
#>        160         64        200    0.972           1.000                0.000^
#> 
#>   ^ The population lies in H0: the rejection rate is the type I error rate.
#>   Approximate power: the share of 20,000 draws of the subjects' sample
#>   mean and covariance in which the test rejects H0, at alpha = 0.05.

# The same design under weaker correlations
usdt_power(update(pop, cor_dprime = c(0.1, 0.2)), subjects = 80,
           trials = c(awareness = 64,
                      influence = 200), dichotomize = "influence")
#> ── Power ────────────────────────────────────────── approximate · 2 scenarios ── 
#> 
#>   H1: Δd' = 0, two-sided test
#>   H2: rho = 0, two-sided test
#>   H3: intercept = 0, two-sided test
#> 
#>   Scenario  Subjects  Awareness  Influence  Δd' = 0  rho = 0  intercept = 0
#>          1        80         64        200    0.656    0.080          0.998
#>          2        80         64        200    0.684    0.188          0.996
#> 
#>   Approximate power: the share of 20,000 draws of the subjects' sample
#>   mean and covariance in which the test rejects H0, at alpha = 0.05.

# \donttest{
# Check the design by simulating and analysing 50 studies (under a
# minute). A real check needs more, e.g. nsim = 1000 with ncores = 2.
sims <- usdt_power(pop, subjects = 80,
                   trials = c(awareness = 64, influence = 200),
                   dichotomize = "influence", method = "simulation",
                   nsim = 50, seed = 1)
sims
#> ── Power ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── simulation ── 
#> 
#>   Design       80 subjects; trials per subject: 64 Awareness, 200 Influence (split at the median)
#>   Reliability  Awareness 0.543, Influence 0.738
#> 
#>   Hypothesis        Test              True      SE  Estimable   Power   MC SE
#>   H1 Δd' = 0        Two-sided test   0.150   0.060      1.000   0.780   0.059
#>   H2 rho = 0        Two-sided test   0.300   0.168      1.000   0.460   0.070
#>   H3 intercept = 0  Two-sided test   0.261   0.045      1.000   1.000   0.000
#> 
#>   Simulated power: the share of 50 simulated studies, each analysed
#>   with hsdt(), that reject H0 at alpha = 0.05 (Monte Carlo SE at most 0.070).
#>   summary() reports the precision of the estimates.

# Bias, empirical and model standard errors, interval width and coverage
summary(sims)
#> ── Precision ──────────────────────────────── 50 simulated studies per design ── 
#> 
#>   80 subjects; 64 Awareness and 200 Influence trials
#> 
#>   Quantity    True   Mean   Bias  Emp. SE  Mean SE  Width  Coverage  Estimated
#>   Δd'        0.150  0.163  0.013    0.067    0.059  0.231     0.880         50
#>   rho        0.300  0.345  0.045    0.161    0.168  0.641     0.960         50
#>   intercept  0.261  0.262  0.000    0.050    0.046  0.182     0.940         50
#>   slope      0.257  0.299  0.042    0.152    0.162  0.636     0.960         50
#> 
#>   Width and coverage are those of the 95% intervals of usdt_tests(),
#>   over the studies that estimate each quantity.
# }
